claims.text: As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and yield strength.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
The relatively low hardness and strength are governed by a dislocation structure lacking effective pinning obstacles.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a metastable, simple solid solution.
The initial alloy contains a relatively free or unoptimized dislocation structure.
Approximately 10% cold work generates a high dislocation density.
A short anneal near 600 °C for 10 minutes can rearrange the generated dislocations into stable, pinned configurations.
The treated microstructure will have increased densities of pinned and reconfigured dislocations.
Pinned and reconfigured dislocations act as effective barriers to subsequent dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation glide enhances work hardening.
The reconfigured dislocation network increases compressive yield strength and hardness.
The pre-strained and annealed alloy will have higher hardness than the as-cast alloy.
The pre-strained and annealed alloy will have higher compressive yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
The strengthening treatment will retain acceptable ductility and sufficient plasticity for machinability.
Excessive annealing can cause recovery that negates the beneficial dislocation reconfiguration.
Treatment conditions outside the proposed window may induce short-range ordering or secondary-phase precipitation.
The proposed mechanism applies under compression from approximately 25 °C through 600 °C while the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution.
Failure to obtain statistically significant increases in both yield strength and hardness accompanied by a changed dislocation network would falsify the proposed mechanism.
